tagline.text: A quiet fishing town in northwest Bohol with the Banacon mangrove forest and the Danajon Bank double barrier reef

location.label: Location
location.text: Northwest coast of Bohol, about 75–90 km northwest of Tagbilaran

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–5,000 (per day; about ₱500–1,500 with local boats, about ₱4,900 for a guided kayak tour)

children.text: Getafe is a small fishing town on the sea at the northwestern tip of Bohol. Its islands include the man-made mangrove forest of Banacon and the Danajon Bank, the only double barrier reef in the Philippines, giving you a quiet side of Bohol that is nothing like crowded Panglao.
Getafe is a local town of about 33,000 people on the northwest coast of Bohol, made up of 24 barangays (villages). Wikipedia puts it about
92 km
from Tagbilaran, while another guide says about
75 km
, so sources differ and it is safest to allow generous travel time. You will often see signs spelled "Jetafe" locally.

Getafe's biggest sights are not on the main island but out on the water. Its islands include Jandayan, Banacon and the western part of Mahanay, and the Danajon Bank, known as the only double barrier reef in the Philippines, runs through the area. Nasingin and Pandanon are small islands described as among the most densely populated in the world.

The best-known place for travelers is the mangrove forest on Banacon Island. Residents began planting bakauan (Rhizophora) seedlings in the late 1950s, and the area is given as anywhere from about 425 hectares to the 480-hectare range depending on the source. Many sources call it the largest man-made mangrove forest in Asia, but that claim has not been independently verified, so treat it as a local description only.

Getafe has almost no tourist facilities, which some people love and others find disappointing. Unlike Panglao, with its hotels and resorts, there are few places to stay and eat, and you should arrange boats and guides in advance. On the other hand, you can cross directly by ferry from Mactan or Cebu City, which makes it a good starting point for a loop around Bohol beginning in the north. The best plan depends on your goal. For photos and scenery, a half-day mangrove paddle is enough; for time on the sea, a full-day trip by rented boat to the sandbars and reef zone near Pandanon suits you better. Official tourism information on this area is scarce and figures differ between records, so please confirm the latest details at the local tourism office or your accommodation before you go.

This large mangrove forest was planted by residents over several decades. Paddling a small boat or kayak along the narrow channels, you can see clear water between the roots and creatures such as shells and shrimp. About 200 households are said to live on the island.
The operator IslandBuzz runs an all-day kayak and SUP route of about
8 km
through the Banacon sanctuary. It is reported to run year-round at about
per person for groups of 2 to 10, but this is older information, so confirm current prices and schedules when booking.

This is the only double barrier reef in the Philippines, running between Getafe's islands. Snorkeling is said to be possible in some sections, but there are almost no facilities, so always go with a local boatman or guide.

This small island lies within the Danajon reef and is known for a long white sandbar and the surrounding sea. You can see fishermen selling fish and sea urchin straight from their boats. There is no timetable for the crossing, and times vary with the weather and currents.

A distinctive fishing community with houses packed tightly onto a tiny island. It is less a tourist spot than a place to see residents' daily life up close, so always ask permission before taking photos.
A hill in Barangay Corte-baud, described as the highest point in Getafe. It is known for sunset views, but no official trail information was confirmed, so ask locals for directions as you climb.

blocks.title: Morning fish landing at Getafe port

children.text: Fishing boats are said to bring in fish and sea urchin at the port between about 5:30 and 8:00 in the morning. There is no fixed timetable, so it may vary with local conditions.

blocks.title: Santo Niño church and a walk through town

children.text: Getafe's parish church is dedicated to the Santo Niño (Holy Infant), and the town fiesta is said to be held on the last Saturday of January. Walk around the market and eateries near the port to enjoy the modest town atmosphere.

items.title: Half-day course
items.subtitle: Getafe port and the mangrove forest

children.text: Stroll around Getafe port, watch the morning fish landing and have a light breakfast.
Board a local boat to Banacon Island from the port. Fares and travel time vary between guides and are reported at about
20–45 minutes
, so check with the boatman before leaving.
Explore the mangrove channels and the village with a guide from the Banacon community group.
Return to Getafe and have lunch at a restaurant near the port.
At low tide the roots are fully exposed, and at high tide the channels are deeper. Tides differ from day to day, so decide your timing together with your guide.

items.title: Full-day course
items.subtitle: Danajon Bank islands and mangrove kayaking

children.text: Travel to Getafe from Tagbilaran or Panglao.
Rent a boat at the port and cross toward Pandanon to see the sandbar and fishing village.
Rest and try fish or sea urchin sold by island fishermen. Check hygiene with your own eyes before eating.
Move on to Banacon Island and explore the mangrove forest by kayak or small boat.
Return to Getafe port, watch the sunset and head back.
Plans in the Danajon Bank area change easily with sea conditions. Schedule your return to the port before dark.
There are flights from Manila (NAIA) to Bohol–Panglao International Airport (TAG), taking about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Flights change by season, so check a booking site.
From the airport, it takes about
2–3 hours
by bus or van via Tagbilaran to Getafe.
You can also fly from Manila to Cebu (MCIA) and cross by ferry.
Getafe's port is a ferry port linked with Cebu. Reported routes are Clemer from Cebu Pier 3, OceanJet from Cebu Pier 1 and Sunriser from Cordova port on Mactan, taking about
1 hour 15 minutes–2 hours
The

The port has minimal facilities and is exposed to the sea, so afternoon sailings are sometimes cancelled in the rainy season.
At the Tagbilaran integrated terminal, take a bus or van heading along the northern coast (toward Talibon) and get off in Getafe. Reports differ widely, at about
1 hour 30 minutes–3 hours
Vehicles toward Talibon often pass through Getafe, but check routes and fares locally.

items.title: Getting around town and to the islands

children.text: Tricycles and habal-habal (motorcycle taxis) are available at the port. Few taxis run in town, so arrange a vehicle in advance if you need one.
Islands such as Banacon and Pandanon are reached by hiring a local boat from the port, and there is no fixed timetable.
Bohol's relatively dry season runs from December to May, which is best for sea trips. Statistically Getafe gets the most rain in November and is driest in April.
Average daytime temperatures are around 28–31 degrees. Typhoons can affect the area from July to September, so always check the forecast and port notices before crossing to the islands.
Birds are most active at dawn and early morning in the mangroves, and the soft light is good for photos. There is little shade at midday, so bring water and a hat.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Cool and mostly clear, with calm seas on many days
Best for mangrove tours and island crossings.
Hot and dry, driest in April
The sun is strong, so a hat and sunscreen are essential.

Getafe has limited tourism infrastructure, so there are few places to stay. The easiest approach is a short trip as a day tour from your hotel in Panglao or Tagbilaran; if you stay overnight, check the latest information and book ahead.

Food is mostly seafood, as you would expect in a fishing town. Reported local dishes include tuyom (sea urchin roe eaten with rice or eggs), squid adobo cooked in its ink, and grilled milkfish (bangus) and spider conch (saang). On Pandanon, fishermen sometimes sell fish and sea urchin directly to boats. Check the freshness and hygiene of raw seafood before eating.

For a day trip, you can cross from Cebu on a morning ferry, see the Banacon mangroves and return on an afternoon ferry. As noted above, sailings can be cancelled, so allowing an extra night gives peace of mind. The most common and cheapest way to eat is at a small eatery (carinderia) near the port, where you choose rice and side dishes. Buy water and snacks at the port before going out to the islands.
Visits to Banacon are said to be guided by the community group BAFMAPA. A guide is recommended; contact details may be out of date, so confirm them at a local tourism office.
The boats are small fishing boats, so check first that life jackets are available, and if not, it is safer not to board.
Mangroves are protected by law, so do not break branches or take wood.
Tides change how much of the roots are exposed and which channels a boat can enter, so match your timing with your guide.
Mobile signal is weak in places, so carry enough cash and download offline maps.
The port is basic, so confirm the last sailing to Cebu and arrive with time to spare.
Island villages are living spaces for residents, so ask permission before taking photos.
Before leaving, ask the municipal tourism contact in Getafe or the Bohol tourism office for boat and guide contacts so you are not left searching on arrival.
Boats to the islands have no timetable and depend heavily on weather and currents. Do not push on during typhoon season or on days with high waves.
Ferries to Cebu can be cancelled on rainy-season afternoons. Leave plenty of margin for a same-day return.
Tourist facilities and emergency medical care are limited. Bring basic medicine and drinking water.
Fares and travel times differ by source, so the figures in this guide are approximate. Check the latest information.
Do not use boats that are not properly licensed.
For the security situation in nearby areas, check the travel safety notices of your government.
